# Yosh Tadbirkorlar Chempionati (Youth Entrepreneurs Championship)

## About
Yosh Tadbirkorlar Chempionati (YTCH) is an annual national competition organized under Presidential Decree PQ-59, designed to support young entrepreneurs aged 18-30 in Uzbekistan. It is the largest youth entrepreneurship investment championship in the country.

Website: https://www.tadbirkorlar-chempionati.uz/

## Key Facts
- Full name: Yosh Tadbirkorlar Chempionati 2025
- Country: Uzbekistan (O'zbekiston)
- Target age group: 18-30 years old
- Prize pool: Up to $10,000,000 (1 billion Uzbek soums per winning project)
- Number of winners: Up to 100 projects
- Grant: Up to 100x BHM (base calculation amount) for marketing and financial services
- Application period: April 27 – May 31, 2025
- Finals: July 15–30, 2025
- Awards ceremony: August 20, 2025
- Legal basis: Presidential Decree PQ-59

## Competition Timeline
1. Registration & Applications: April 27 – May 31, 2025
2. Round 1 & Results: June 1–10, 2025
3. Round 2 & Results: June 10 – July 10, 2025
4. Final Round: July 15–30, 2025
5. Awards Ceremony: August 20, 2025

## Application Categories
1. An'anaviy biznes (Traditional Business) — For existing businesses seeking to scale and become major Uzbek companies
2. Startap (Startup) — For tech and innovation solutions with a clear problem-solution fit seeking investment to grow faster
3. G'oya (Idea) — For promising ideas with strong potential seeking to become real products, launch MVP, and attract investment

## Benefits for Winners
1. Up to 1 billion Uzbek soums investment per project
2. Up to 100x BHM grant covering marketing and financial services
3. Brand building through media, TV, and public promotion
4. Title of "Yosh Chempion Tadbirkor" (Young Champion Entrepreneur)
5. Recommendation for state awards: "Faol tadbirkor" and "O'zbekiston belgisi" badges
6. Internships at prestigious international accelerators and companies

## Prohibited Categories
- Alcohol-related businesses
- Tobacco-related businesses
- Any activity contrary to Uzbekistan law

## Rules
- Each participant may only enter one project
- Team members cannot participate in multiple teams

## Appeal Process
Participants may submit an appeal within 3 days of results being announced.

## Partners & Sponsors

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is the investment a loan?
A: No. The investment is an equity contribution to the project's charter capital. The form varies — direct equity, convertible financing, or mixed financing with a grant element.

Q: What can the investment be used for?
A: Allowed: equipment, software, MVP development, marketing, certification, export preparation, specialists, working capital. Not allowed: repaying prior debts, dividends, personal expenses, prohibited activities.

Q: What happens after winning?
A: An investment agreement is signed and funds are disbursed in a lump sum or in tranches. Winners submit quarterly reports and projects are monitored against KPIs.

Q: What if KPIs are not met?
A: The next tranche may be suspended, investment terms reviewed, or the contract terminated. In serious breaches, funds may be recovered under applicable law.

Q: Is my idea confidential?
A: Yes. Submitted business plans, financial models, and trade secrets are not disclosed to third parties.

Q: Can I apply without a registered business entity?
A: Yes, individuals may apply as citizens — with the condition that a business entity must be established upon winning.

Q: How are projects evaluated?
A: By soundness of business model, market potential, financial stability, team competence, innovation level, technological readiness, job creation potential, export potential, and ability to attract additional private investment. Evaluation is done in two stages — document review and pitch presentation.

Q: How do I submit an appeal?
A: Within 3 working days of results being announced, a written or electronic appeal may be submitted to the Fund. The Fund responds within 10 days.

Q: Can a team apply together?
A: Yes. A team may apply as a legal entity — however, at least 50% of the charter capital must belong to an entrepreneur aged 30 or under.
